title: One Obstruction, Three Faces — Merle Lean stack, with Lean 4 formalisations of Halbeisen–Hungerbühler 1997, Lagarias 1990 and Steiner 1978
description:
Lean 4 verification stack of Eric Merle (the “kernel key”) for the joint note One obstruction, three faces with Benjamin Macindoe, together with Lean 4 formalisations of two classical papers: L. Halbeisen and N. Hungerbühler, “Optimal bounds for the length of rational Collatz cycles”, Acta Arithmetica 78 (1997), 227–239, and J. C. Lagarias, “The set of rational cycles for the 3x+1 problem”, Acta Arithmetica 56 (1990), 33–53; and of a classical theorem, R. P. Steiner, “A theorem on the Syracuse problem”, Congressus Numerantium 20 (1978), 553–559, reconstructed from published accounts, proved under a named hypothesis in steiner1978/ and without it in logs23/.

hh1997/ (Lean 4.34.0, Mathlib v4.34.0): every result that the paper proves is kernel-checked (70 proved statements, each frozen before its proof was written), with no sorry in the proofs, no native_decide, and only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. One statement of the paper, Remark 1 for l > 10³, is stated and not proved, since the paper gives no proof; Remark 2 and two figures the paper quotes from other authors are not formalised. The formalisation proves nothing new about Collatz cycles. See hh1997/README.md, which also lists the points found in the paper.

lagarias1990/ (Lean 4.34.0, Mathlib v4.34.0): 60 frozen statements, all proved (61 theorems, since Corollary 2.1a is proved twice), each statement written before its proof (git records this order for the last six), with no sorry in the proofs, no native_decide, and only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Theorem 3.1 with the printed constant and Theorem 3.2 are proved under named hypotheses (the prime number theorem; the bound (3.3), a consequence of the Baker–Fel’dman bound), which are hypotheses of the theorems, not axioms; Theorem 3.1 is also proved without any hypothesis, with the constant 6/5 instead of 5/4. Out of scope: Theorems 3.3 and 4.3, the bounds (4.12)–(4.14), Remarks (2)–(4) of p. 52 with (4.19), and the flat segment of Fig. 4.1. The minimality of the 48 unchanged rows of Table 3.1 is checked numerically, not in Lean. For the results in scope, where we found a slip in a printed statement or proof, the repaired version is proved; the slips found are listed next to what is printed in lagarias1990/README.md, and the list is not exhaustive. The formalisation proves nothing new about Collatz cycles.

steiner1978/ (Lean 4.34.0, Mathlib v4.34.0): the statements and the proof were written without the original paper; they are reconstructed from R. Steiner, Fibonacci Quarterly 19 (1981), 285–288, J. C. Lagarias’s annotated bibliography of the 3x+1 problem (entries 48, 158, 159) and J. Simons and B. de Weger, Acta Arithmetica 117 (2005), read in their version 1.44 (2010), §1.4 and Lemma 12. After release v1.2, on 2026-10-21, the paper was read in a scanned copy and compared with the statements: nothing in the Lean files changes (steiner1978/README.md, section Comparison with the original). Release v1.2 said that the original paper could not be accessed, and the frozen header of steiner1978/Steiner/Steiner_Enonces.lean (line 10, unchanged in this release) says that it was not available to us; these claims are withdrawn (steiner1978/README.md, Related work). 12 frozen statements, all proved, each statement written before its proof, with no sorry in the proofs, no native_decide, and only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Steiner’s theorem (the only circuit on the positive integers that is a cycle of the 3x+1 map is {1, 2}) is proved under a named hypothesis, the case u₀ = 0 of G. Rhin’s inequality (7) (Progress in Mathematics 71, 1987), called H_Rhin in the Lean files, which is a hypothesis of the theorems, not an axiom. Without any hypothesis it is proved, in steiner1978/, for at most 20000 odd terms, by a finite check certified by the kernel; this is far weaker than the published bounds that rest on computer verifications of the conjecture. It is proved without this hypothesis in logs23/ (below). The formalisation proves nothing new about Collatz cycles.

logs23/ (Lean 4.34.0, Mathlib v4.34.0; new in v1.4): Steiner’s theorem without the hypothesis H_Rhin. The proofs of steiner1978/ use H_Rhin only to bound the number k of odd terms, and what they need is much weaker: 1/(2^k − 1) ≤ |(k + l) log 2 − k log 3| for every k > 20000 and every l ≥ 0, which logs23/ proves. For k below 6.34·10^100 this follows from two consecutive convergents of log₂ 3, with enclosures of log 2 and log(3/2) computed by the kernel; for k ≥ 2^334, from an explicit, deliberately crude lower bound exp(−10^12 ν^5) ≤ |b₁ log 2 − b₂ log 3| for every natural b₁ and every natural b₂ ≥ 2^334, ν = ⌊log₂ b₂⌋ + 1, proved, after division by the gcd of b₁ and b₂ (small reduced denominators are handled by the convergents), with an interpolation determinant in the spirit of M. Laurent (Acta Arithmetica 66, 1994) and a positivity argument (Cauchy–Binet, Descartes’ rule of signs) in place of a zero lemma. Hence the statements steiner, steiner_int, steiner_cycle, steiner_cycle_int and tstar_circuit of steiner1978/ hold without their premise; in particular, with no hypothesis, the only circuit on the positive integers that is a cycle of the 3x+1 map is {1, 2}. 14 frozen statements, all proved, each statement written before its proof, with no sorry in the proofs, no native_decide, and only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Not proved: H_Rhin itself (Rhin’s paper is not formalised); the sixth statement of steiner1978/ with the premise H_Rhin, rhin_k_le, is not restated without it. The bound is far weaker than the published explicit bounds (Laurent 1994; M. Laurent, M. Mignotte and Y. Nesterenko 1995; N. Gouillon 2006). No novelty is claimed: replacing the zero lemma by positivity may well be known. The formalisation proves nothing new about Collatz cycles.

The rest of the repository is the Merle side of the joint note; the status of each of its entries is the claims ledger of the shared repository macindoe/one-obstruction-three-faces, not this archive. Its six ledger Lean files (OneObstruction/) were first checked on Lean 4.27.0 and re-checked on Lean 4.34.0 (recheck-v4.34/RECHECK.md); recheck-v4.34/Labo/ holds lab modules offered for information (Lean 4.34.0; one sorry, the marker of the open target T★). Nothing in this repository excludes a Collatz cycle beyond the published bounds (Bařina's verification to 2^71; Hercher 2023).

v1.5 (documentation only): adds the file LICENSE, the official legal code of CC BY 4.0 (releases v1.0 to v1.4 contain no LICENSE file; their license is the one stated in their README and Zenodo record), a CITATION.cff file, a section of the root README on re-checking the formalisations of classical papers from a fresh clone, and dated notes in the READMEs. No Lean file, check script or recorded axiom report changes.

Source repository (with the git history cited in the READMEs): https://github.com/ericmerle3789/one-obstruction-three-faces-lean. Website: https://collatz-lab.org. License: CC BY 4.0.
